verdict: First in the FAA paperwork, confirmed. Whether the failure technically started there is still unclear. The Air Current, citing airline sources, reports the outage was first reported at Chicago Center, then Boston, Washington, New York and Minneapolis in rapid succession, after which the FAA went nationwide. That sequence is reported, not an official center-by-center log, and is consistent with a propagating common-network failure rather than 22 independent collapses. The 2014 Aurora fire is a poor comparison: that was a single-building loss, neighboring centers absorbed the airspace, and there was no nationwide stop.
confidence: High on the paperwork; sequence reported, not official

verdict: The 70% upgraded figure is confirmed: L3Harris's FTI page says 70% of sites were upgraded as of Nov. 2, 2026, and the FAA said on Nov. 5 that 69% of copper wires had been replaced. That work is on the current FTI network; FENS is a separate AT&T next-generation planning order from August 2026. A cutover causing today's outage is unverified: no public cutover schedule or contract change names Nov. 13, and L3Harris says it switches over during low-traffic windows. L3Harris had no comment as of 6:46 PM ET, per CBS.
confidence: High on the 70% figure; cutover unverified

verdict: Still sourced reporting only. Officials now give a cause on record: Duffy says overloaded legacy TDM switches and routers, and Mullin says new equipment overwhelmed the older system and that it "appears this was mechanically driven." That fits an upgrade-related trigger but does not confirm a software update, a reboot or L3Harris. Reuters, citing two airline officials, says the affected network is the L3Harris-overseen one carrying controller radio; L3Harris did not comment. CBS (an update caused a reboot and crash) and Bloomberg (FBI looking at a software update, one unnamed person) stay Reported. The FAA newsroom still says "communication issues." A Saturday Hindustan Times explainer, citing Bloomberg and people familiar with an FAA industry briefing, says some of the equipment was already running over capacity, that once it was overwhelmed the failure spread to the old telecom backbone, and that L3Harris has been asked to diagnose the overload. Those two Bloomberg details could not be independently confirmed in a Bloomberg text story, L3Harris has not commented, and the FAA has not confirmed them; they stay Reported/unconfirmed.

verdict: Debunked as a nationwide NWS/NEXRAD or radar.weather.gov outage. NWS said there is no radar outage, that radar.weather.gov is working, and that outdated isolated webpages caused the confusion. The circulating "nation-wide internet and communications issues" notice was stale Los Angeles office page text, archived as early as December 2025; the page now returns 404. NCEP said at 6:01 PM ET Friday that all radar data systems and network communications were normal. NWS offices in Birmingham and Huntsville said NEXRAD dataflow was nominal and that FAA comms issues had not affected NWS operations. Narrower and confirmed: a few airport terminal Doppler weather radars (TDWR) had brief Friday dropouts — Newark 12:19–12:44 PM ET and Milwaukee 12:46–3:53 PM ET — and when Boston's airport weather-radar feed was restored at 3:46 PM ET, NWS Boston noted that Boston Center had reported telecom issues. That is the FAA problem touching one feed, not a national Weather Service outage. Duffy's inconsistent radar data refers to FAA ATC radar feeds on the overloaded telecom network, not NWS weather radar.

Canadian systems were not hit, per official statements. NAV CANADA and Transport Minister Steve MacKinnon both said Canadian systems are operating normally. What stopped were US-bound flights, plus some flights that would cross US airspace. NAV CANADA added traffic management at Toronto, Montreal, Calgary and Vancouver. Calgary said US-bound departures were held, with no other impacts. Porter grounded flights that would cross the US on the way to Mexico and the Caribbean.
confidence: High, based on statements, not an inspection of the systems

verdict: Some international departures observed around 6 PM are now officially corroborated: FAA Advisory 001, issued 7:37 PM ET, says some coastal facilities released international departures under a nationwide ground stop with selective releases. Specific Hacker News flight numbers remain unverified. Other leads are unchanged: a secondhand pilot account that radar and pilot radio are up and the break is the center-to-center data handoff; an AT&T-provides-the-ARTCC-network claim that is partly true at most (AT&T's FENS award is a $74.3M planning task; L3Harris still operates FTI; nothing public links AT&T to today's outage); and a 911-systems-down rumor that is unconfirmed (no official nationwide outage; Downdetector user reports from 4:13 PM ET are unverified; Lincoln, NE and Tulare, CA lost only non-emergency lines). Click2Houston quotes Mullin saying DHS and CISA are looking at whether SMART contributed; that role is not established.
confidence: Mixed: international releases confirmed; other items observational or rumor
